goals.detail:
### Queued: the hero walks onto a floor square holding more than one object

Set aside on 31 July 2026 when `scripts/scan-debt.mjs` landed. The scan rates
this behavior 383 screens of `supports` and 61 of `unlocks` in one session,
`seed0004-feeding-pony`, against 188 for `#levelchange`. Slice 1 was drafted and
never validated; that draft is parked on the branch `wip/object-pile-window` and
no line of it is verified against the C source.

A walking hero steps onto a square holding two or more objects with
`!autopickup`. `pickup.c pickup()` takes its `(autopickup && !flags.pickup)`
early return into `check_here(FALSE)`, the run stops, and `invent.c
look_here()` opens the `Things that are here:` window.

In scope: the `look_here()` branches reachable when the square holds more than
one object and no guard requiring `Blind`, `u.uswallow`, `is_pool`/`is_lava`,
`visible_region_at()`, a seen trap, `will_feel_cockatrice()` or a nonzero
`dfeature_at()` holds -- the `otmp->nexthere` window (`invent.c:4288-4313`) and
the `skip_objects` count line (`4251-4276`) that `flags.pile_limit` selects --
plus `pickup()`'s no-autopickup arm and its `nomul(0)` run stop. Excluded:
`autopick()` and `pickup_object()`, the whole autopickup arm.

`invent.c look_here()` (4104-4315) is already ported apart from those two
branches, and `js/pickup.js check_here()` is live at `js/hack.js:1158` behind
`domove_core()`, so the consumer exists. The work is widening
`requireSimpleHeroDestination()` (`js/hack.js:414-444`) and finishing
`look_here()`'s `'the object-pile menu'` throw at `js/invent.js:454`. Roughly
150 new C lines, two or three slices.

**Why it was selected, and what replaced that reasoning.** Over 60 freshly
generated D:1 levels (seeds 7100000-7100059) the port produces 19.4 squares
holding an object per level, in 100% of levels, and 1.28 squares holding a
*pile*, in 72%, against 1.12 traps, 0.75 fountains and 0.10 sinks. Object
squares outnumber every other unported destination class by an order of
magnitude, and 20 of 33 development sessions set `!autopickup`. That argument
measured incidence on a generated level, which no development session samples.
`scripts/scan-debt.mjs` measures the recorded sessions themselves and reaches a
different answer: one session needs this owner, and it earns 61 screens there.

`seed0004-feeding-pony` stops here at 26 of 409 steps.

**The `flush_screen()` question, traced but not yet recorded.** Whether the
pile window trips the menu-erasure defect under `## Unresolved` was left open
when this goal was queued. A source trace says it does not. `pline.c:274`'s
`if (u.ux) flush_screen()` is the only such call inside `vpline()`, and between
`create_nhwindow()` and `destroy_nhwindow()` at `invent.c:4288-4313` there is
no `pline()`, `You()` or `There()` -- only `putstr()`, `doname_with_price()`
and `display_nhwindow()`. `check_here()`'s own `flush_screen(1)`
(`pickup.c:451`) runs before the window opens. The one message that can follow
is `read_engr_at()`'s, after `destroy_nhwindow()` has already repaired the
corner through `docorner()`, and `js/hack.js:453` refuses an engraving on an
admitted square regardless. The defect's two known victims are menu *search*
prompts, which a window with no menu items cannot reach. That is a trace, not
evidence; slice 1's differential converts it, and converts it automatically,
because a wrong reading shows up as a mismatched pile screen.

**Slices.**

1. *The window itself.* A walking hero's one-square step onto a ROOM or CORR
   square holding two to four objects, ending at the dismissed
   `Things that are here:` window and the next command prompt. Upstream:
   `look_here()`'s final `else` arm (`invent.c:4288-4313`) and its tty
   realization -- `wintty.c tty_putstr()`'s NHW_MENU case (2360-2410, with
   `compress_str()` and the `n0 > CO` line break), `tty_display_nhwindow()`'s
   NHW_MENU arm, `dmore()`, and `tty_dismiss_nhwindow()` into
   `erase_menu_or_text()`'s `docorner(offx, maxrow + 1, 0)`.
2. *The count line.* `skip_objects` at `invent.c:4251-4276`
   (`There are two/a few/several/many objects here.`), which `flags.pile_limit`
   selects, plus explicit non-default settings including `pile_limit:0` and
   `pile_limit:1`. Message only; no window, and none of slice 1's rendering.
3. *A pile on a decorated square.* Lifting `js/hack.js:445`'s
   `terrain feature description` refusal for a staircase or doorway holding a
   pile, which adds the `dfeature` header `putstr()` pair at 4291-4294 and its
   blank separator. This merges with the separately listed hero-destination
   stop for a decorated square holding an object, whose `dfeature_at()` and
   `stairs_description()` are ported already.

The count line is second rather than first because the default `pile_limit` is
5: an ordinary walk meets a two-to-four pile, and a pile of five or more is the
rarer case that "complete common gameplay first" defers.

**Where slice 1's difficulty sits: rendering, not game logic.** Three traced
hazards, recorded here because each is invisible until it is fatal.
`tty_display_nhwindow()` routes this NHW_MENU to `process_text_window()`
because `cw->data` is non-NULL, while still using *menu* geometry --
`offx = max(10, cols - maxcol - 1)`, `offy = 0`, `dmore()` offset 2 and the
`(end)` prompt -- so neither `renderTtyMenu()` nor `displayTtyTextWindow()` is
the right donor alone; the port needs the first one's layout and the second
one's line loop. `maxcol` is `strlen(str) + 1` after `compress_str()`,
maximized over every line including the heading, and one character off shifts
the window a column and misses every cell in it, discontinuously, because
`offx === 10` flips to a full-screen clear. And `tty_putstr()` splits a line
wider than `CO` at the last space before column 79 and re-submits it, adding a
row and changing `maxcol`, before `display_nhwindow()` computes any layout.
`js/tty_menu.js:340` `displayTtyTextWindow()` hardcodes `offx = 0`;
`dismissTtyMenu()` (`js/tty_menu.js:278-311`) already models the
`maxrow + 1` repair that erases the `(end)` row, and is the better donor for
it. `display_nhwindow(WIN_MESSAGE, FALSE)`'s
`toplin == TOPLINE_NEED_MORE -> more()` arm has no owner in the port at all.

goals.detail:
### The hero's experience level rises

**The bounding property, testable against the C source.** C code is in scope
exactly when it runs while `u.ulevel` increases and is reached from
`wizcmds.c wiz_level_change()`'s `newlevel > u.ulevel` arm or from
`exper.c newexplevel()`. Code that runs only while `u.ulevel` decreases is out:
`exper.c losexp()` (207-297) and `wiz_level_change()`'s `newlevel < u.ulevel`
arm stay fail-closed. No recorded session lowers a level.

**What the goal gates.** A capped ceiling of 128 recorded steps across the five
sessions stopped on `#levelchange`; `scan-debt` rates the same owner 1,785
screens of `supports` across those five. All five sessions' next unmet command
after the stretch is `wizlevelport` (`^V`), so this goal opens the wizard-mode
level-teleport sequence for a later goal. It also deletes the `goto_level() as a
Tourist reaching a new level` refusal at `js/do.js:661`, which stands in front of
the Tourist descents in `seed0900`, `seed5006` and `seed0030`'s second life.

**Upstream owners and how much C.** `wizcmds.c wiz_level_change()` 444-486 (43
lines); `exper.c pluslvl()` 305-376 (72), `more_experienced()` 167-201 (35),
`newexplevel()` 298-305 (8); `attrib.c` innate tables 23-105 (83 lines of data),
`adjabil()` 1004-1073 (70), `role_abil()` 787-816 (30), `postadjabil()` 778-787
(10), `setuhpmax()` 1155-1177 (23); `botl.c xlev_to_rank()` 296-310,
`rank_to_xlev()` 313-330, `exp_percentage()` 2050-2083 and
`exp_percent_changing()` 2088-2124 (mostly `STATUS_HILITES`-gated and
unreachable); `weapon.c add_weapon_skill()` 1435-1451, `give_may_advance_msg()`
74-86; `insight.c record_achievement()` 2405-2472, `count_achievements()`
2492-2501, `achieve_rank()` 2504-2512. Roughly 380 live C lines plus the 83-line
table.

**What the port already has.** `exper.c newuexp()` and `newpw()` are ported in
`js/exper.js`; `attrib.c newhp()` at `js/attrib.js:99`; `weapon.c can_advance()`
and `slots_required()` at `js/weapon.js:841-863`; `display.c see_monsters()`,
which `postadjabil()` calls for `HWarning` and `HSee_invisible`, at
`js/display.js:1833`; `dungeon.c level_difficulty()`; and `tty_getlin()` at
`js/getline.js:328`, so the `To what experience level do you want to be set?`
prompt has an owner. `js/extcmdlist_data.js:81` already holds the `levelchange`
row with `WIZMODECMD`, and `js/cmd.js:212` and `:1105` already gate wizard-mode
rows, so the only missing wiring is a `case 'wiz_level_change'` in the dispatch
switch at `js/cmd.js:1138-1165`. `u.ulevelmax`, `u.ulevelpeak`, `u.uhppeak` and
`u.uenpeak` all exist in `js/u_init.js`.

**Traced findings that shape the work.**

- `pluslvl()`'s `Upolyd` arm (`monhp_per_lvl()`, `setmhmax`) is unreachable:
  `js/u_init.js` is the port's only writer of `u.umonnum` and sets it equal to
  `u.umonster`.
- `pluslvl()`'s `Welcome back to experience level %d.` arm is unreachable on a
  rising path: `u.ulevelmax` is bumped inside the same block, so every recorded
  line reads `Welcome to experience level N.`
- Message order is load-bearing for the random-number log.
  `You_feel("more experienced.")` prints before `newhp()` and `newpw()` consume
  `rnd()`/`rn1()`, `++u.ulevel` and the `Welcome` pline follow, and `adjabil()`
  runs last. The recorded streams confirm it: at level 15 `seed0360` reads
  `You feel sensitive!  You feel more experienced.--More--`, the intrinsic line
  trailing level 15's welcome and sharing a top line with level 16's opening.
- `add_weapon_skill()` prints nothing in any of the five sessions because
  `can_advance()` also requires
  `P_ADVANCE(skill) >= practice_needed_to_advance(...)`, and a hero who has
  struck nothing has zero practice, so `before == after`. The slot increment is
  still real state.
- `livelog_printf()` writes a file the port cannot write and reaches no screen,
  matching the treatment already recorded at `js/do.js:658-660`.
- Rank achievements do fire: `xlev_to_rank(20)` is 5, so a 1-to-20 change records
  `ACH_RNK1` through `ACH_RNK5` into `u.uachieved[]`. No screen output, but it is
  saved state.
- Hazard: `postadjabil()` calls `see_monsters()` when `HWarning` or
  `HSee_invisible` changes -- levels 15 (Wizard, Priest, Caveman, Healer), 7 and
  15 (Monk), and 15 (Ranger). `js/display.js:1852` and `:1864` throw on a long
  worm and on a warning artifact, neither of which these levels hold, but the
  warning-glyph path through `newsym()` is untested, and that file's header
  comment saying no level change is ported goes stale with this goal.

**Indicative slices** (the slice-selector decides the real division).

1. *The command and one level gain.* `wiz_level_change()`'s prompt, parse, and
   its equal and raising arms; `pluslvl()` with `setuhpmax()`; the welcome line
   and the status line. `adjabil()` and the lowering arm stay fail-closed.
2. *The intrinsics a level grants.* The innate tables, `adjabil()`,
   `role_abil()`, `postadjabil()`, `add_weapon_skill()`.
3. *Rank achievements.* `record_achievement()`, `count_achievements()`,
   `achieve_rank()`, `rank_to_xlev()`.
4. *Experience points from play.* `more_experienced()`, `newexplevel()`,
   `exp_percent_changing()`, wired to the Tourist arm at `js/do.js:661`, deleting
   that refusal.

**Why this goal and not the queued pile window.** Re-ranked at `af2b7335` by the
capped look-ahead forecast `.agents/selection.md` requires. Six candidates were
capped with `scripts/scan-ahead.mjs` and a classifier holding the port's boundary
and command sets: `#levelchange` 128 (5 sessions, no stretch cut), pet ranged
targeting 33 of a raw 370 (4 sessions, an eleven-fold cut on combat, a trap and a
count prefix), door or special terrain movement 31 (3, uncut), `#twoweapon` 21 of
35, movement while riding 10 of 31, and the floor object pile 1 of 61. Hero or
monster combat caps four of the six; `#levelchange` is the only candidate whose
stretches hold no second unported behavior, so nothing has to be priced in. It
wins on both ranking keys -- highest capped forecast and most sessions stopped --
so no tie-break applies.

goals.detail:
### The hero enters a furniture square

`rm.h:138` defines `IS_FURNITURE(typ)` as `typ >= STAIRS && typ <= ALTAR`, which
is this goal's whole subject: stairs, ladders, thrones, fountains, sinks, graves
and altars. The hero reaches one by walking, by running, or by swapping with the
ordinary starting pet standing on it.

**The stop is measured, not inferred.** Replaying each session and catching the
boundary with `onBoundary` on `runSegment()` puts the two `seed0013` sessions at
`js/hack.js:627` inside `requireSimpleHeroDestination()`, hero at (34,15),
refused destination (35,15), `typ=30` = `SINK` (`js/const.js:77`), with
`context.run === 1`. `seed2600` stops at `js/hack.js:885` inside
`requireOrdinaryStartingPetSwap()`, refused destination (60,3), `typ=26` =
`STAIRS`, occupied by the kitten. One census row, two seams, two terrains. C's
recorded screen confirms the sink: the hero stands on the `{` at the next step
with an empty top line.

**C reaches almost nothing new, which is why the refusal is the whole cost.**
`hack.c test_move()`'s chain has no arm for furniture -- `IS_OBSTRUCTED` is
`typ < POOL` (`rm.h:119`) and `IS_DOOR` is false -- so an orthogonal step falls
through to `testdiag` and is admitted. The run stop at `hack.c:2936-2941`
(`IS_DOOR || IS_OBSTRUCTED || IS_FURNITURE(tmpr->typ)`) is already ported at
`js/hack.js:1461-1466`. `hack.c spoteffects()` (3312-3480) has exactly one
furniture arm, `IS_SINK(...) && Levitation -> dosinkfall()` at 3353-3354,
unreachable without levitation; its tail below the `pickup(1)` at 3381 holds only
the ice warning and the hidden-monster surprise, both refused ahead of it.
`pickup.c:702-709` returns before `look_here()` on an object-free square, running
`describe_decor()` only under `flags.mention_decor` and then `read_engr_at()`.

**Where the work actually sits.** Two sibling guards are written against
`STAIRS || doorway` and must be restated against the same predicate, or widening
`ordinaryDestination` silently admits cases they were holding: `js/hack.js:636-639`
(`'decor description'`) and `js/hack.js:653-656` (`'terrain feature
description'`). `invent.c dfeature_at()` is already ported (`js/invent.js:161-230`)
and covers fountain, throne, sink and grave through the cmap; its ALTAR arm throws
for `a_gname()` and its ice arm for `ice_descr()`, so ALTAR needs those helpers or
an explicit refusal. A temple altar is already bounded: `js/rooms.js` refuses
`check_special_room()` entering room type TEMPLE.

**The pet swap has no terrain condition in C.** `hack.c domove_swap_with_pet()`
(2098-2180) tests the pet's trapped state, its diagonal ability, a boulder on the
hero's square, `bad_rock()`, and `goodpos(u.ux0, u.uy0, mtmp, 0)` for the square
the *pet* moves into. It never tests the square the hero moves onto.
`js/hack.js:879-888`'s ROOM/CORR/D_NODOOR list is a seam artifact that lags the
walk seam, which already admits STAIRS.

**Incidence, as context and explicitly not as a forecast.** Over 80 freshly
generated D:1 levels (seeds 7300000-7300079, Valkyrie, datetime 20290418073000)
the port's own generator produces 1.09 non-stairs furniture squares per level,
with 68% of levels holding at least one: fountains 0.80, sinks 0.15, altars 0.07,
graves 0.06, and no thrones or ladders on D:1. `docs/goal-history.md` demotes
fresh incidence to nomination only, and records that the pet-inventory goal was
chosen on fresh incidence alone and returned a holdout zero. It is here only to
say which terrain the first slice should cover -- the fountain -- and that ladder
and throne belong last or stay refused.

**Why this goal and not the field.** Capped look-ahead on 2 August 2026 across
twelve candidates: this boundary 31 (3 sessions, no stretch cut), `apply` 26 (2),
`#twoweapon` 24 of 35 (1), `#pray` 21 (1), pet ranged targeting 20 of 370 (4),
`fire` 17 (1), monster trap activation 16 (1), `wizlevelport` 14 of 95 (4),
`takeoff` 14 (2), movement while riding 10 of 31 (1), and the floor object pile 1
of 61 (1). Pet ranged targeting stops the most sessions but its four stretches cap
on four different unported behaviors -- graffiti, `#ride`, hero combat and a count
prefix -- so its sessions buy the shallowest follow-on in the field.

**Indicative slices** (the slice-selector decides the real division).

1. *The walk onto a bare fountain or sink.* Widen the seam to `IS_FURNITURE()`
   and restate the two sibling guards. Closes on both `seed0013` sessions plus a
   fresh differential over a fountain and a sink.
2. *The ordinary-pet swap onto furniture.* Closes on `seed2600`.
3. *Grave and altar.* Includes `dfeature_at()`'s `a_gname()` arm or its explicit
   refusal, with the case just outside the limit being an altar inside a temple.

goals.detail:
### Clearing the `commands` deferral backlog

`npm run quality -- deferrals` reports `commands` holding ten open entries
outside the `scope` category, which is the threshold `.agents/selection.md`
sets for a deferred-area sweep. A sweep takes precedence over any fail-closed
boundary port until the area drops below it, and each open entry is already a
slice, scoped when it was deferred, so this goal needs no slice selection.

The ten, as at `e3a3d1d`:

1. `the status line repaints on every turn, where C gates it` (production)
2. `u_on_newpos() drops earth_sense() with no refusal` (production)
3. `a drawbridge wall answers "It's a wall."` (production)
4. `three arms of the door message switch are dormant` (production)
5. `the m prefix loses a frame` (production)
6. `go.occupation has one writer and three readers that never see it`
   (production)
7. `movement-path-has-no-failclosed-wrapper` (production, slice)
8. `eight diagonal-doorway findings are deferred` (clarity)
9. `the two-meal segment never reaches its second meal` (tests)
10. `adjabil()'s already-held suppression test has no reachable case` (tests,
    slice, and blocked on `#wizintrinsic`)

**Order.** Two of the ten are fail-open rather than fail-closed, meaning the
port skips a message-writing C branch silently instead of stopping: entries 1
and 2. `AGENTS.md` singles that out as the one thing an unported path must not
do, so they come first. Entry 1 leads because it sits on a line that runs every
turn of every session and its own record calls it the first
emitted-and-wrong screen the project would produce; entry 2's branch is dormant
for a narrower reason that is now written down, that every burial site on a
reachable level is a GRAVE or STONE square which `earth_sense()` rejects before
reading the buried list.

Entry 10 cannot close inside this goal: it waits on `#wizintrinsic`, which no
goal has ported. It stays open and the area stays at nine until then, which is
below the threshold.

**What a sweep is worth.** Nothing in recorded steps, by construction: every
entry names behavior no development session reaches, which is why each was
deferred rather than fixed. The forecast is recorded as 0 for that reason, not
as a guess. Entry 1 is the exception in one direction -- it changes rendering
on a line every turn draws, so it can move the score either way and needs its
own differential and a whole-score comparison rather than an audit-fix line.

forecast.basis: capped look-ahead, 2 August 2026, over the two sessions the wish stops: seed0360-wizard-world-tour 90 of 90 and seed0108-wizard-extcmd-wishlist 16 of 16, neither cut. Step-level streams hold only the tty_getlin echo and the result line, and the recorded random-number log across all four wishes names only rnd_otyp_by_namedesc, next_ident, mksobj_init, blessorcurse and makewish's rn1(100,50). Highest of eight candidates; pet ranged targeting caps at 36 of 373 over five sessions. Note that 90 of the 106 are the getlin echo, whose owner is already ported.

goals.detail:
### A wizard-mode hero wishes for an object

**The bounding property, testable against the C source.** The wish text reaches
`readobjnam_postparse3()`'s `rnd_otyp_by_namedesc(d->actualn, d->oclass, 1)`
(`objnam.c:4749-4759`) and matches exactly one `objects[]` entry, after
`readobjnam_preparse()` consumed only a count, a `blessed`/`cursed`/`uncursed`
word and a `+N`/`-N` enchantment, and `readobjnam_postparse1()` consumed only a
class word. The created object is not an artifact, corpse, statue, figurine,
egg, tin, glob, fruit or container; the hero has a free inventory slot and is
not `Fumbling`, so `hold_another_object()` takes its plain `addinv` tail.

**Read the forecast correctly.** 106 capped steps across two sessions, both
uncapped, but 90 of them are `seed0360`'s `tty_getlin()` echo, and
`tty_getlin()` is already ported at `js/getline.js:328`. The goal unlocks a long
stretch of replay for a modest amount of new behavior. That is a good trade and
not a large-behavior forecast; judge the delivered figure against it knowing
where the steps come from.

**Upstream and how much C.** 1,854 lines by exact span: `wizcmds.c wiz_wish()`
32-44; `zap.c makewish()` 6314-6422; `objnam.c readobjnam()` 4910-5400,
`readobjnam_init()` 3933-3961, `readobjnam_preparse()` 3966-4175,
`readobjnam_parse_charges()` 4178-4237, `readobjnam_postparse1()` 4240-4663,
`readobjnam_postparse2()` 4666-4724, `readobjnam_postparse3()` 4727-4899,
`wishymatch()` 3243-3338, `rnd_otyp_by_namedesc()` 3455-3529;
`invent.c hold_another_object()` 1208-1306 and `prinv()` 2875-2890. Most is
refused rather than ported. The in-scope path is the `preparse` qualifier arms,
`postparse1`'s class-word extraction, `postparse2`'s `makesingular`,
`postparse3`'s four `rnd_otyp_by_namedesc()` calls, and `readobjnam()`'s
`typfnd:` tail. This goal needs a checklist under `AGENTS.md` and closes over
several slices.

**What the port already has.** `tty_getlin()` (`js/getline.js:328`); `mksobj()`
(`js/obj.js:1451`), `mksobj_init()` (`js/obj.js:1191`), `blessorcurse()` and
`next_ident()`; `addinv()` (`js/invent.js:1850`); `donameFresh()`
(`js/objnam.js:773`); `mungspaces()`; `encumber_msg()`; and the `objects[]` and
`obj_descr[]` tables. Missing entirely: `readobjnam` and its chain,
`wishymatch`, `rnd_otyp_by_namedesc`, `hold_another_object`, `prinv`,
`makewish`, `wiz_wish`.

**Traced findings.**

- The wish-history machinery is dead in the comparison build.
  `wish_history_add()`, `wish_history_menu()` and `wish_history_flush()` are each
  inside `#ifdef DEBUG` (`zap.c:6229`, 6261, 6277), and `config.h` defines only
  `DEBUG_MIGRATING_MONS` at 620, with no patch under `nethack-c/patches/`
  defining `DEBUG`. So `wish_history[0]` is always NULL and `makewish()`'s

goals.detail:
### A wizard-mode hero teleports to a numbered dungeon level

**The bounding property, testable against the C source.** `wiz_level_tele()`
runs with `wizard` set; `level_tele()` takes the
`(Teleport_control && !Stunned) || wizard` arm; `getlin()`'s answer is a decimal
string for which `lev_by_name()` returns 0 and `atoi()` a positive `newlev`;
`single_level_branch(&u.uz)` and `In_quest(&u.uz)` are false and `next_to_u()`
is true; `get_level()` resolves `newlev` inside dnum 0 to a level whose
`level_info[].flags` lacks `LFILE_EXISTS`; and `goto_level()` runs with
`at_stairs`, `falling` and `portal` all FALSE, reaching `u_on_rndspot(0)`.

**Out of scope.** The `?` menu (`print_dungeon()`), `*` and the
`random_levtport` arm, negative levels with their heaven, Nowhere and `done()`
paths, the `In_endgame` arm, the non-wizard `Teleport_control` route,
`level_tele_trap()` and `mlevel_tele_trap()`, and any destination that is a
special level or one already generated.

**Read the forecast correctly.** 180 capped steps, and 174 of them are the
already-ported `getlin()` echo and wish-result lines. The six genuinely new
screens are the prompt, its echo and the arrival in each of the two sessions.
The forecast therefore rests on the just-closed wish path holding across four
object classes it did not exercise: wand, ring, scroll, and tool or container. A
divergence in any one wish truncates the rest of that session, so judge the
delivered figure knowing that most of it is replay the goal unlocks rather than
behavior it adds.

**Upstream and how much C.** About 550 lines read, roughly 230 of them in-scope
arms to translate, which is comparable to the descent goal and smaller than
`wizard-mode-wish`'s parser. `wizcmds.c wiz_level_tele()` 399-406;
`teleport.c level_tele()` 1164-1440, the wizard positive-number arm only;
`do.c schedule_goto()`, `deferred_goto()` and `goto_level()`'s `!at_stairs` arm
1802-1810; `dungeon.c get_level()`, `lev_by_name()`, `single_level_branch()` and
`u_on_rndspot()` 1604-1638; `mkmaze.c place_lregion()`, `put_lregion_here()`,
`bad_location()` and `is_exclusion_zone()`; `mklev.c occupied()` 1806-1812; and
`allmain.c moveloop_core()` 538-539.

**Traced findings.**

- `js/do.js goto_level()` is the descent port, and the arrival arm this goal
  needs is one refusal to lift: `js/do.js:540-544` throws
  `'goto_level() arriving without stairs'`. The `up` refusal at 545-550 does not
  fire, because both destinations are below D:1.
- A prerequisite rather than a widening. `js/mklev.js:200-238` already carries
  `place_lregion()` and `bad_location()`, both commented "simplified for
  skeleton". `bad_location()` omits C's `occupied()` (`mklev.c:1806`) and the
  `AIR` term, and `put_lregion_here()` is absent altogether. The `LR_DOWNTELE`
  arm is what a level teleport uses, and it relocates a monster standing on the
  chosen square through `rloc(mtmp, RLOC_NOMSG)` and `m_into_limbo()`, but only
  on the deterministic pass; the probabilistic pass retries instead, spending
  two `rn1()` calls per try. The existing helper is wrong for this caller as
  written.
- `next_to_u()` is ported at `js/apply_next_to_u.js` and answers TRUE for an
  ordinary hero with a pet, so `level_tele()`'s `You1(shudder_for_moment)` guard
  passes without new work.
- `schedule_goto()` and `deferred_goto()` have no port. `js/allmain.js:777`
  already refuses the other call site, `allmain.c:385-386` inside the monster
  loop; the one this goal needs is `allmain.c:538-539`, after `rhack()`.
  `wiz_level_tele()` returns `ECMD_OK`, so no time passes and no monster moves
  between the command and the arrival: the whole transition happens inside one
  keystroke.
- `dungeon.c get_level()`, `lev_by_name()` and `single_level_branch()` are
  absent from `js/dungeon.js`. For a numeric answer `lev_by_name()` runs only
  its `find_mapseen_by_str()` leg, the port keeping no mapseen chain per
  `js/do.js:454-459`, then `find_level()` (ported at `js/dungeon.js:803`) and
  `find_branch()`, and returns 0, so `atoi()` supplies `newlev`.
- Both destinations are ordinary levels, measured rather than assumed. Booting
  the port for each seed and reading `game.dungeon_topology`: seed5002 places the
  Oracle at D:8, the Mines branch at D:4 and Sokoban at D:9, so D:5 carries no
  special map and no branch; seed5006 places its Mines branch on D:2, the level
  it teleports to, so `place_branch()` (`js/mklev.js:3181`) runs on arrival. Both
  sit inside what the descent goal validated: 2,347 of 2,347 fresh descents
  reached a drawn D:2 (`docs/goal-history.md:34`,
  `scripts/run-leave-level.mjs`).
- The `?` menu is deliberately out of scope. It is `dungeon.c print_dungeon()`,
  three pages of branch and special-level rows including the castle tune. The
  only two sessions that use it spend the selection on a level `mklev()` cannot
  build, so including it buys 3 screens in seed0383 and 4 in seed0373 and then
  stops.
- The census hides a cap here, and it is a destination rather than a prompt.
  seed0383 is cut from 95 to 0 at step 42 and seed0373 from 85 to 0 at step 43:
  both answer the prompt with `?` and select a Lua special level, `e - bigrm: 12`
  and fakewiz1 at 46, that `mklev()` cannot build. seed0373's Amulet wish at
  steps 104-106, an unmodelled fifth route into `makewish()` through
  `allmain.c:445-449`, sits behind that arrival and never becomes the binding
  cap. The general caution stands: the debt model classifies commands, so a
  prompt-answering byte can hide an unported behavior.
- `js/wizcmds.js` already ports `wiz_wish()` and `wiz_level_change()`, so
  `wiz_level_tele()` belongs in that file, and `js/extcmdlist_data.js:167`
  already carries the `0x16 wizlevelport` row. The entry point is
  `ADMITTED_COMMANDS` at `js/cmd.js:711`, the list the current boundary message
  recites.

**Why this goal and not the field.** Capped look-ahead on 3 August across eleven
candidates: this boundary 180 over two sessions, pet ranged targeting 36 of 373
over five, `#twoweapon` 21 of 35, `apply` 21 of 26, movement while riding 10 of
31, the floor object pile 1 of 61, and fifteen others whose uncapped ceiling is
22 or less, which no capping read can raise above the runner-up. Pet ranged
targeting carries the highest raw figure and was set aside on arithmetic alone:
four separate unported behaviors sit inside its five stretches, cutting 373 to
36, which is below even the last closed goal's delivered 106. This goal was
preferred at five times that capped figure and because it opens a capability the
port wholly lacks, arriving on a level other than by walking down a staircase,
which `.agents/selection.md` names as the property that has moved the holdout.

**`object-pile-window` was re-ranked, not opened.** Its capped figure is 1 of 61,
in the single session seed0004-feeding-pony, and the census's 61 is a projection
of that one session's remaining input rather than a second measurement. Its
queued entry keeps its slice plan and `flush_screen()` trace, and sits behind
this goal.

**Calibration.** The three most recent non-sweep goals delivered 1.00, 0.90 and
1.00 of their capped forecasts, so 180 should be read as a genuine expectation
rather than the upper bound `unlocks` used to be.

goals.detail:
### Ordinary starting pets evaluate distant targets

The source-bounded capability is the target-selection pass reached from dog_move() for an active starting kitten, little dog, or pony. best_target() scans eight rays through find_targ() to distance 7 and score_targ() ranks a visible ordinary target. The three fixed starting species have only AT_BITE or AT_KICK followed by AT_NONE; score_targ() rejects adjacent targets. A selected target therefore reaches only mattackm()'s distant physical-attack miss path and the pet may continue moving. Real AT_WEAP, AT_BREA, or AT_SPIT attacks, special or confused pets, minions, priests, vampshifters, melee, retaliation, and displacement remain outside this goal and fail closed.

The current port already owns find_targ() in js/dogmove.js. The missing coherent group is dogmove.c find_friends(), score_targ(), best_target(), and pet_ranged_attk(), plus dog_move()'s call. Roughly 328 C lines define that targeting group. mhitm.c mattackm() is larger in full, but this boundary reaches only its setup and distant bite, kick, and AT_NONE miss projection. That narrow source-named port belongs in js/mhitm.js and must preserve source quirks even though the attack misses: wake a helpless target, set visibility, assign magr->mlstmv to moves, clear skipdrin, and return M_ATTK_MISS without a to-hit draw. mhitu.c getmattk() substitutions cannot fire for the three fixed species.

Fresh scan-sessions and look-ahead classification at c27653f cap the raw 394-step ceiling to 42 across five sessions: seed0030 contributes 15 before pet combat, seed0103 14 before pony combat, seed0200 6 before hero combat, seed0900 4 before pet combat, and seed2600 3 before the still-partial level-teleport question-mark route. One ambiguous byte inside those stretches is the already-supported #ride prompt. This boundary opens those later pet-combat, hero-combat, and print_dungeon boundaries without claiming them.

Runner-up apply carries 26 uncapped steps across two sessions, below 42 over five. The queued object-pile-window remains behind this goal because its raw 61-step stretch caps at 1: bear-trap activation follows the Things-that-are-here window immediately.

goals.detail:
### The hero applies a tool

`apply.c doapply()` (4214-4430) is the `a` command. Its entry is short — `nohands()`, `check_capacity()`, `getobj("use or apply", apply_ok, GETOBJ_NOFLAGS)`, `retouch_object()`, then three `oclass` shortcuts (wand, spellbook, coin) and a switch on `otyp`. Two arms of that switch carry the whole forecast: `STETHOSCOPE` at 4327-4329 and `LOCK_PICK` at 4290-4293. Everything else in the switch is the goal's boundary and must stop at a named refusal, including `SACK` reaching `use_container()`, which the Rogue also carries as inventory letter `f`.

**The stop is measured.** Both sessions stop on the port's repeated-command boundary refusing the byte `a` (`js/cmd.js:783-786`, `ADMITTED_COMMANDS` at 717-720). The scan puts `seed0016` at 3/36 and `seed0077` at 18/33, and both stretches were read step by step against the recorded keys, not from the top-line summary.

**Most of the scaffolding is already ported.** `getobj()` is `js/invent.js:369` and already serves `eat`, so `apply_ok()` plugs into an existing consumer rather than needing one. `getdir()` is `js/cmd.js:515`, `confdir()` is `js/cmd.js:496`, `check_capacity()` is `js/hack.js:255`, and `nohands()` is `js/mondata.js`. `js/lock.js` already owns `lock.c`'s `xlock` context, `reset_pick()` and `maybe_reset_pick()`, and its header comment names `pick_lock()` as the deliberate gap, so `pick_lock()` lands in the file that is already waiting for it.

**Three things are genuinely new.** `insight.c ustatusline()` (3402) has no port; `js/insight.js` is its owner. `freehand()` has no port and gates `use_stethoscope()`'s third guard. `svc.context.stethoscope_seq` compared against `gh.hero_seq` (decl.c:394, allmain.c:260 and 396) is the free-action rule that decides whether the first stethoscope use of a move costs time; `state.hero_seq` already exists (`js/u_init_inventory_attrs.js:237`, validated at `js/allmain.js:428`), so only the `stethoscope_seq` half is missing, and it needs one owner.

**`retouch_object()` needs a decision before the first commit.** `js/eat.js` references it but `js/` has no port; `QUALITY.json` carries `artifactTouchable() crashes a segment instead of ending it` against the same area. Neither starting kit holds an artifact, so the branch is dormant for both sessions, but it sits between `getobj()` and the switch and must be ported or refused explicitly rather than skipped.

**A branch neither starting character reaches.** `use_stethoscope()`'s `u.usteed`, `u.uswallow`, `u.dz` and cursed-object arms (346-378) are all unreachable here: `.` zeroes all three deltas and both stethoscopes are `{ STETHOSCOPE, 0, TOOL_CLASS, 1, 1, 0 }`, uncursed by definition at u_init.c:79. `pick_lock()`'s resume-an-interrupted-attempt branch (378-400) needs `gx.xlock.usedtime`, which `reset_pick()` is the port's only writer of and which is zero on a first application.

**A side effect worth pricing in.** `pick_lock()` is half of what `QUALITY.json`'s `an explicit autounlock setting is refused` says its fix belongs with, the other half being `autokey()`. Porting it does not close that entry — the entry waits on the parser for `flags.autounlock` — but it removes the `door unlocking tool` refusal at `js/hack.js:986-988` from the critical path, which is what currently caps `seed0007`'s `options` stretch at step 50.

**Why this goal and not the field.** Capped look-ahead on 6 August 2026 across fourteen candidates: this boundary 26 over two sessions with neither stretch cut, `#twoweapon` 25 of 35, `#pray` 21 of 21, pet combat evaluation 19 of 21, `takeoff` 18 of 18 over four, `fire` 17, monster trap activation 16, `options` 16 of 48, hero combat 15 over two, `wizgenesis` 11, riding movement 10 of 31, hero trap activation 8 of 61, engraving interaction 6 of 238, `#rub` 2 of 22. `options` led on the raw figure and on a first reading of its stretch, and it lost on the second: `seed0007` picks `lit_corridor` among its eight booleans, and `options.c:5362-5375` answers that option with `vision_recalc(2)`, `gv.vision_full_recalc = 1` and, because `color` is on and its address is `&iflags.wc_color` (optlist.h:236-238), `go.opt_need_redraw = TRUE`. `js/vision.js:746` skips at `control === 2` exactly the loop C runs there, and `reglyph_darkroom()` and `check_gold_symbol()` have no port at all — `js/do.js:855-864` and `:910-916` record both as deliberately unreachable. That caps `options` at step 36, where the picks are applied.

goals.detail:
### Clear the monsters area's deferral backlog

`npm run quality` at `0d3e6d3` names `monsters` at ten open non-`scope`
deferrals, and `.agents/selection.md`, "Deferred-area sweeps", requires
resolving one of an area's entries before the next boundary goal opens. Read
every entry in the area first; the reading costs more than the closing.

**Order.** The rule orders entries by how the port behaves at each one: an
entry where the port silently skips a message-writing C branch comes before one
where the port stops at a named refusal, because `AGENTS.md` forbids the first
and permits the second.

By that order the silent divergences lead:

- `gremlin-in-a-fountain` (production, small). Both `minLiquid` owners answer
  false for a fountain, so `mon.c:961 minliquid_core()`'s gremlin split at
  `:987` never draws its `rn2(3)`. Closable today by refusing.
- `artifactTouchable() crashes a segment instead of ending it` (production).
  `js/weapon.js:264-268` throws a bare `TypeError`, which costs the whole
  session prefix rather than ending the segment on its last matching screen.
  Same shape as `dosounds-refusal-escapes-as-hard-failure` in `world-effects`
  and `a live monster refusal escapes as a hard failure` in `startup`.
- `will-weld-ported-twice` (simplification, small). `js/wield.js:18-27` and
  `js/weapon.js:520-527` hold independent ports of `wield.c will_weld()` and
  `erodeable_wep()`. Opened by the `apply-tool-command` correctness pass, which
  applied the cross-reference comments and left the convergence here because
  `js/weapon.js` sat outside its reviewed range.
- The two planning-clone entries, `leaks by omission` and `must copy
  non-enumerable catalog aliases`. Both concern
  `preflightSimpleMonsterActions()`'s clone, which the next boundary goal will
  exercise hard whichever one is chosen.
- `one pickup assertion still does not discriminate` and `nine postmov findings
  are deferred`, both test-category.

**Expected survivors.** An entry closes only when the behavior its record names
as the closing condition is ported, so three are expected to survive on
